claims.statement: The product is melody-in-heart (applicationId cn.com.dcsgo.mihx), a purely local offline-first Android music player with no INTERNET permission, running Kotlin 2.0.21 + Compose (BOM 2025.09.01) + Media3 1.9.0 (with Jellyfin FFmpeg decoder) + Hilt 2.52 + Room 2.6.1 + DataStore 1.1.1 + WorkManager 2.9.1 + LiteRT 1.4.1, at versionName 3.7.0 / versionCode 33, minSdk 33, targetSdk 36, Java 11 bytecode, split into 14 Gradle modules (:app, :core:model, :core:common, :core:ui, :domain, :data, :player, six :feature:* modules, :benchmark).

verifyProductArchitecture is a custom root-build.gradle.kts Gradle task (~530-line doLast block) registered in the verification group and wired into the root check lifecycle; it statically asserts module boundaries (no :data/:player/cross-feature deps from features, no implementation-layer import leaks), the Hilt entry points and six SingletonComponent DI modules, immutable Room schema snapshots, LazyColumn stable keys, AppLog over android.util.Log, release R8/resource-shrink settings, privacy backup excludes, and PerformanceTrace anchors; the GradleException message names the violated rule.

./gradlew check aggregates the root spotlessCheck, the root verifyProductArchitecture, and every one of the 14 subprojects' own check tasks (each subproject's check also depends on its spotlessCheck covering Kotlin/Kotlin-script/XML formatting); it must be run before committing.

CLAUDE.md and docs/ are valuable but historically lagging references that must be cross-checked against code: CLAUDE.md still lists Compose BOM 2024.09.00 and versionName 3.5.1 (versionCode 29) while gradle/libs.versions.toml has composeBom 2025.09.01 and app/build.gradle.kts has versionName 3.7.0 / versionCode 33; source and tests are the only authority.

The 14-module layering is: :app shell (AppRoot/AppNavHost/AppRoutes/AppDestinations, PermissionCoordinator, emotion scan worker, app-level Hilt modules) depends on all other modules; six :feature:* modules depend only on :core:* and :domain and expose the Route+Screen pattern; :domain holds repository interfaces plus pure playback policy with no Android dependencies; :data owns Room MelodyDatabase and DataStore wrappers with narrow adapters; :player owns AppMediaSessionService, PlaybackController, windowed queue planning, Bluetooth coordination, and EmotionAnalyzer support; :core:model/common/ui hold pure data types, logging/trace, and shared Compose components.

Offline and privacy invariants: the app manifest declares only POST_NOTIFICATIONS, FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK and BLUETOOTH_CONNECT (no INTERNET); library import uses SAF document-tree access and verifyProductArchitecture forbids declaring READ_MEDIA_AUDIO/READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE; backup/data-extraction rules must exclude playback state, Room files, DataStore files, and the album-art cache; notification and Bluetooth permissions may only be requested from user-triggered Settings paths, never at startup (startup-path requests fail the architecture task).

Room persistence is MelodyDatabase v10 with 13 entity classes (songs, playlists, playlist-song cross-ref, play stats, playback events, quick-skip songs, quick-skip short plays, song group overrides, migration state, artists, albums, song-artist cross-ref, song_emotions) and exportSchema=true with JSON snapshots 1.json..10.json under data/schemas/; DatabaseModule registers MIGRATION_1_2 through MIGRATION_9_10 and provides SharedPreferencesLegacyJsonMigration for the first-launch v1 SharedPreferences-JSON-to-Room migration; historical schema JSON must never be edited.

Five DataStore preference files complement Room: player_settings (theme, play modes, Bluetooth/notification toggles, lyric font scale, sleep timer, emotion scan pause, mood-time-slot master switch), playback_state (playback snapshot persistence, owned by :player's PlaybackStateStore with a legacy music_player_prefs SharedPreferences), playlist_resume (per-playlist resume JSON), mood_time_slot (time-slot configs as a single-key JSONArray), and emotion_failures (per-song failure JSON with attempts counting); all are excluded from backup.

Emotion batch scanning is scheduled from MelodyApplication.onCreate via EmotionScanScheduler as a WorkManager unique periodic work (emotion_periodic_scan) every 6 hours under charging + battery-not-low constraints with a 30-minute initial delay and NetworkType.NOT_REQUIRED; the periodic EmotionScanWorker analyzes up to 40 pending songs per run while the manual trigger (manual=true one-time work, unique name emotion_manual_scan) analyzes up to 300 per run and auto-enqueues the next batch with APPEND semantics.

EmotionAnalyzer (:player, @Singleton) runs a MediaCodec/FFmpeg decode to 16k mono PCM then 5s-window/2.5s-hop YAMNet embedding averaging into emotion_va_head.tflite producing per-window valence/arousal curves and whole-song mean, using the two TFLite models in :player assets with MODEL_VERSION yamnet-va-v3; failures carry a displayable EmotionFailureReason, are persisted to EmotionFailureStore, and songs accumulating MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 failures stop being auto-retried.

Analysis results persist in the Room song_emotions table (SongEmotionEntity: valence, arousal, curveJson of raw per-window values, peakSec, windowsAnalyzed, durationSec, modelVersion, base64 1024-dim embedding, plus userValence/userArousal/userTags calibration fields) through SongEmotionsRepository implementing the :domain SongEmotionRepository interface.

Mood time-slot semantics: MoodSlotResolver (:domain, pure logic, independently unit-tested) treats configs as left-closed/right-open [start, end) intervals with end <= start meaning cross-midnight, picks the earliest-starting hit on overlap, and validates saves (name length, non-empty tags, zero-length, pairwise overlap) by throwing IllegalArgumentException; PlayerRandomQueueFacade evaluates the active slot per random-play request and filters candidates by emotion tags at the planner entry, falling back to full-library random when the filtered pool is empty and warning when it is below MoodSlotPolicy.POOL_WARN_THRESHOLD=10.

PlayerViewModel is a deliberately thin @HiltViewModel facade delegating to PlayerRuntime, a composition root that lazily assembles five graph objects (PlayerQueueGraph, PlayerMediaControllerGraph, PlayerPersistenceGraph, PlayerBluetoothGraph, PlayerPlaybackSessionGraph) and eighteen per-concern facades; the old PlayerViewModelComponents assembly hub was deliberately dismantled and verifyProductArchitecture fails the build if any file references it again.

Queue invariants: PlayQueue.songs is the full business queue (duplicates allowed; currentIndex indexes into it) while MediaController only holds a windowed plan whose size stays between 51 and 71 items (20 before + current + 50 after, clipped at queue edges) for 100/500/1000-song libraries as locked by PlaybackWindowPerformanceShapeTest; SongMediaItemMapper sets MediaItem.mediaId to Song.id.toString() as the mapping contract back to the business queue; navigation goes through MediaController, not PlayQueue index arithmetic.

Build variants: debug (no minification, applicationIdSuffix .debug so it coexists with release), release (R8 minify + resource shrink, arm64-v8a only, resConfigs zh/en, falls back to debug signing without keystore.properties unless -PrequireReleaseSigning=true makes the build fail), and benchmark (initWith release but debug-signed, non-debuggable, adds x86_64 for emulators); :benchmark is an Android-test (com.android.test) module targeting :app with StartupBenchmark (cold-start StartupTimingMetric) and ScrollBenchmark (FrameTimingMetric) run via :benchmark:connectedCheck.

Navigation: AppRoutes defines the Navigation Compose route table (home, playlist, playlist/{id}, artist/{name}, album/{name}, user, settings, lyrics, playback-stats, song-top-list, version-management, emotion-analysis, mood-time-slot, etc.) and AppDestinations maps the three bottom tabs (PLAYLIST/HOME/USER) including sub-page to tab attribution, recomputed from the active back-stack route so tab highlight stays correct; app-shell ViewModels including MoodTimeSlotViewModel must be created at Activity scope in AppRoot, because creating them inside NavHost composable blocks falls back to a non-Hilt factory and crashes.

Test tiers: JVM unit tests (./gradlew test, no device) live in domain/, player/, data/, feature/*/, core/* and app/ test sourcesets covering planners, synchronizers, repositories and facades; instrumented Compose tests (HomeScreenComposeTest, PlaylistScreenComposeTest, SettingsScreenComposeTest, RuntimePermissionPolicyTest) run via :app:connectedAndroidTest on an emulator/device; Macrobenchmarks run via :benchmark:connectedCheck with EMULATOR suppression for x86_64 simulators, though MIUI ROMs may block them.
